notes: Round-2 before/after proof, run live 2026-09-21 against the plan coffee-pilot-round2 declared 2026-09-03. Same yardstick as every prior window, one copy each: handoff_minutes under the T-11 operational definition and the T-12-passed measurement system. Before is the round-1 pilot window (after-round1.csv, n=120, mean 6.198 -- the implemented state since 2026-08-24), so the Welch test isolates what the grinder change itself added; the CUMULATIVE claim is the gap block, which runs final state against the original measured baseline 8.408333 per R-IMP-03 (per-change credits stay descriptive, never summed). After is the full declared pilot window (after-round2.csv, n=120, all 10 mornings, no trimming). The declared season/demand confounders are re-answered YES against actuals and the engine prints the weakened sentence on the verdict -- the direction of the bias (semester demand is ~15% MORE load) means the confound could only have masked improvement, not manufactured it, and the note travels with the number. Guardrails are the charter's two consequential metrics on their charter-baseline before-values, so the guardrail read is cumulative too. Capability of the after-window (Cpk 0.054 against USL 5.0) is the honest close: the mean promise is met, the every-order promise is not -- recorded in improve-run.md with the /stats/baseline run. The pilot's declared_package is echoed verbatim (R-IMP-02's carve-out), so the verdict itself carries package-level attribution: the win belongs to the dosing-method package as a whole -- the dial-in routine plus the standby grinder -- never to either component alone.

declared_package.rationale: The dial-in routine and the standby grinder are one inseparable dosing-method change: a mid-peak swap is impossible without a second dialed-in grinder standing by, and a second grinder is pointless without the routine that keeps both units dialed in. Separate them and neither is testable alone -- a routine with a single grinder still stalls the line on every drift, and an un-dialed standby just moves the re-dial wait to a different machine -- so the pilot deploys the package whole and attribution stays package-level.
components: Pre-peak dial-in routine: dial in the primary grinder before 7:00 and re-dial after every hopper refill, logged on the grinder card
Pre-dialed standby grinder: when the primary drifts mid-peak, swap in the standby unit instead of re-dialing while cups wait

plain_language.comparison_summary: Compared before (n=120, mean=6.198) against after (n=120, mean=4.899) using Welch's two-sample t-test (unequal variances assumed by default -- no equal-variance check to trip on).
plain_language.p_value_meaning: p = 0.0000, below the alpha=0.05 threshold: if there were truly no difference, a result at least this far from 'no difference' would turn up by chance alone only about 2.2e-27% of the time. That makes the difference statistically detectable here -- it does not mean the null hypothesis is false with that probability, and it says nothing yet about whether the difference is big enough to matter.
plain_language.effect_size_in_words: Cohen's d = 1.69 -- a large difference (Cohen 1988 conventional bands: negligible<0.2, small<0.5, medium<0.8, large>=0.8).
plain_language.practical_significance_prompt: Statistically detectable ≠ big enough to matter -- compare the effect size above against the goal.

provenance.method: Welch's two-sample t-test (scipy.stats.ttest_ind, equal_var=False; NIST/SEMATECH §7.3.1 unequal-variance form + Welch-Satterthwaite df) + Cohen's d on the unweighted-average SD (Delacre, Lakens & Leys 2017)
